text.p: French chemical and pharmaceutical company Rhone-Poulenc will report a 1996 net attributable profit figure some 20 to 25 percent higher than 1995's 2.134 billion francs ($372 million), a source close to the company said.
A spokeswoman for Rhone-Poulenc declined to make any comment ahead of the January 30 publication of the figures.

The operating profit will be 25 to 30 percent higher than the 6.223 billion franc 1995 figure and the profit per share will see an increase of just over 20 percent from 6.71 francs last year, the source said.
1996 sales will be up by some two percent from the 84.79 billion francs of 1995.
Rhone-Poulenc net profit in 1996 was hit by nearly $75 million because of the voluntary recall of albumine products of its 50 percent unit Centeon in the United States, the source said.
Jean-Rene Fourtou, chairman for the past 10 years, aims to show an increase of 20 percent in the net per share figure, excluding exceptionals, for 1996, 1997 and 1998.
The source said that Fourtou wants to obtain an operating income of 13 billion francs in 1999.
According to Jacques Chahine Finance, financial analysts are expecting a net attributable profit if 2.686 billion francs, sales of 85.96 billion and a net per share of 8.49 francs.

The 1996 results have been boosted by the pharmaceutical activities with strong sales of the anti-cancer drug Taxotere, thrombosis treatment Lovenox and the anti-inflammatory drug Synercide, the source said.
During 1996, Rhone-Poulenc sold between seven and nine billion francs of non-strategic assets.

While its investments were almost equal to that in 1995, 6.132 billion for industrial activities and 7.059 billion for research and development, the debt to equity ratio will have dropped to about 60 percent in 1996, the source said.
At the end of 1995, the ratio stood at 71 percent and the source said the group hoped to get below the 50 percent level at the end of 1997.
During the year, Rhone-Poulenc will probably try to sell its basic chemicals operations and a part of the fibres and polymers activities, or seek an alliance in these sectors.
On Monday, Rhone closed 2.78 percent higher at 166.60 francs.
